alerts.title: Abdominal pain: possible TDF toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines list abdominal pain or discomfort and decreased appetite as presenting signs of TDF toxicity including lactic acidosis or severe hepatomegaly with steatosis, and recommend performing LFTs and RFTs if these symptoms appear. Patient is on TDF and reports abdominal pain today. Appetite is preserved and there is no fever, which argues against severe toxicity or infection. However, TDF-associated lactic acidosis can present with abdominal pain even before appetite loss. No LFTs or repeat RFTs have been ordered.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform LFTs and RFTs as recommended for TDF toxicity evaluation. If deranged, manage per guideline and consider TDF substitution.

alerts.title: Low-level viremia at 25 copies/mL
alerts.message: Guidelines note that viral load above suppression thresholds is associated with risk of sexual transmission and subsequent virologic non-suppression and treatment failure. Patient's viral load is 25 copies/mL, which is above the target-not-detected level but below the ≤200 copies/mL plasma suppression cutoff. This low-level viremia warrants enhanced adherence monitoring. The clinician's plan does not address the detectable viral load.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess adherence and repeat viral load per algorithm. If persistently detectable, follow VL testing algorithm for potential treatment failure evaluation.

alerts.title: TDF annual creatinine monitoring gap
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for patients on TDF. Patient's last creatinine was 78 days ago, but no documentation confirms this was part of the required annual TDF monitoring cycle. The clinician's plan today does not include renal function monitoring despite new abdominal pain symptoms that warrant RFT evaluation per TDF toxicity guidelines.

evidence.recommended_action: Verify annual creatinine and eGFR monitoring is current. Given abdominal pain, perform RFTs now per TDF toxicity screening guidance.
